It still has a pretty high hallucination score, and I’ve found models high on that benchmark don’t work well for certain workflows.

It’s not just overt hallucinations themselves, but it seems to correlate strongly with a certain “laziness”, poor communication, forgetting/skipping steps, etc.

You can overcome a lot of it by being much more strict in prompts, more detail in plans, etc, but they tend to “cheat”, make assumptions, and/or just imagine details are done and work without checking otherwise.

I mostly just skip models with rates over 80% or so now except for narrow, specialized subagents. The new flash is in the mid 80s. The old ones were mid 90s.

The GPT 5.6 models at max are all up in the 90s, too, and I see the same problems with them.
